fixes.explanation: "Sick" feels close, like you just need a good nap. Paul uses a bigger word: "…you were dead in your trespasses and sins…" (Ephesians 2:1). A sick person is still waiting to get better, and Paul says dead. I think that makes the good news even louder.

Nice thought, but that's not the reason Paul gives. He says, "But because of His great love for us, God, who is rich in mercy…" (Ephesians 2:4). The text names His love, and doesn't say we called out first.

Right on time, and by time I mean the worst possible time. Paul says God "…made us alive with Christ even when we were dead in our trespasses." (Ephesians 2:5). The timing is "even when we were dead in our trespasses." That's some kind of timing.

I get it, we usually figure we have to tidy up before company comes. But Paul says God "…made us alive with Christ even when we were dead in our trespasses." (Ephesians 2:5). The word is "even when," not "once they stopped."
Grace! Paul says, "It is by grace you have been saved!" (Ephesians 2:5). Look at that exclamation point on the end of the line. Grace is the word the verse lands on.
I see why "law" came to mind, it's a big word in the Bible. But Paul says, "It is by grace you have been saved!" (Ephesians 2:5). Grace is the answer, and the verse ends with an exclamation point.
Wisdom is a good thing, but it's not the word in this verse. He says, "It is by grace you have been saved!" (Ephesians 2:5). Grace is the word, and the verse ends with an exclamation point.

Seated, baker! Paul says God "…raised us up with Christ and seated us with Him in the heavenly realms in Christ Jesus…" (Ephesians 2:6). Raised up and seated, both with Christ, in the heavenly realms.

Hid? That's not the word Paul uses, friend. He says God "…raised us up with Christ and seated us with Him in the heavenly realms in Christ Jesus…" (Ephesians 2:6). Seated with Christ is the picture he gives.

A gift! Paul says, "For it is by grace you have been saved through faith, and this not from yourselves; it is the gift of God…" (Ephesians 2:8). Not from ourselves, so it didn't start with us. It's the gift of God, and it comes by grace through faith.
True, baker. Paul says salvation is "…not by works, so that no one can boast." (Ephesians 2:9). Not by works, and the reason is right there in the verse: no one can boast.
I get why you'd think so, but Paul says it differently. The good works are ones "…which God prepared in advance as our way of life." (Ephesians 2:10). The text says God prepared them in advance.

Right, baker. Paul says the good works are ones "…which God prepared in advance as our way of life." (Ephesians 2:10). The text says God prepared them in advance. My own planning is mostly "more chocolate chips."
